vision: You run four heroes from your first day. They hunt on their own while you are away, and you win by preparing them: who stands where, what they wear, what their bars do and where you send them. Harder tiers ask for a real party with roles. Gear is a chase with rare finds worth keeping and showing. Levels never end, and gear, sinks and old grounds keep pace with them by formula, so the long game always has a next step. Around the hunt sits a shared world of clans, world bosses, events and PvP arenas that gives you reasons to know other players. Every number comes from one set of formulas you can read.

ruled.what: All four heroes from the start. No slot prices. (GR-2)
One Premium for each account.
No solo or group balance targets. Party buffs make hunting together the obvious choice. (GR-67)
The MMO layer is clans, world bosses, events and PvP arenas, and it is heavy work going forward.
Decisions first. No build lanes until every decision is made and a build plan exists.
The current game is irrelevant. Nothing is compared with it. Its data is evidence only.
Balance is fixed at the formula layer. No ground, weapon or monster gets its own patch or its own math.
Nothing planned for later is cut. It is built later and stays hidden until it works.
The itemization plan is a source of record.
Every time number assumes a player hunts 12 hours a day, measured in low, mid and best gear, to Level 400.
The Level table is the clock of a mid-geared four on the hardest tier it holds.
Level 400 takes 4,580 hunted hours, which is day 382.
Best gear is about 15% faster and takes about 15% less damage than mid gear.
A death costs 6% of all Level XP, flat, with no cap.
The harder tiers kill at a flat count at every Level. A mid-geared party on Deadly dies 50 to 100 times in 1,000 hours.
The weekly limits on chest opens stay.
120 days of grounds at Early Access, and each region opens 30 days before the first fours arrive.
The Luck bar keeps its hours: +16% at 500 hours, +39% at 5,000.
A player may cost at most $0.15 an account a month at 1,000 accounts, and no more at 10,000.
Bought gold has no limit on how much sooner. The limit is on what can be bought.
Two visits a day is the free game.
Heroes work in town for all 12 rested hours.
A full set of the best gear takes about one band to Krell, then one to two regions.
Crafting is a quarter to a half of the step from mid gear to best gear, and a player who never crafts can buy it.
The too strong and too weak thresholds stand, and any cut goes to you on one list first.
One Global chat, with lines sent in small batches and a slow mode when crowded.
Clan castle goods keep their prices. Only the two goods that cannot be made are fixed.
A unique can be reforged up a band and keeps its property. Each new band also gets uniques of its own.
The every-idle-hour training reading is a number we watch, never a gate.
Faction skills are sized to matter.
Spells are sized first, then Deadly.
Storm and Bone runes unlock at Runecrafting 25 and 40.
Cleave merges into Turning Cut.
Rend stays at 6 seconds and the axes do not hold Power Strike.
Mend heals about 11% of max health.
The hammer has its own strike that spends an Earth rune.
The crossbow has its own spell list. Sixteen Necrotic and Storm spells in all.
Only people are weak to Necrotic.
Every spell is sized at Level 10 and at Level 60, so heals and first strikes land whole in the first hours.
Krell is weeks away, not months: day 18 for a four.
The recommended option of every call in the four dives of 11-20 is approved.
Tempering carries up a tier and costs only the difference.
Generous drops through Krell, really rare and strong after.
Luck has two feeds and no more: rivets used and Bestiary stages.
The harder tiers hit harder, sized on a party with a healer and monsters that shoot the back row.

decideFirst.call: Approve the formula clean-up steps that move no number, and apply a tier's dial once.
decideFirst.whyFirst: Every later number is read through these formulas.

decideFirst.call: The balance matrix is the gate for every balance change, with a band for XP after deaths and party lineups.
decideFirst.whyFirst: Nothing below can be judged on evidence until the measuring tool is true.

decideFirst.call: Town work is paid in closed form. The way an away hunt is saved waits for study 48.
decideFirst.whyFirst: The game has to fit $0.15 an account before any system is added to it.

decideFirst.call: Deadly is sized so a four with a shield tank and a healer holds it, and a four without them does not.
decideFirst.whyFirst: It decides whether preparing a party is a real decision.

decideFirst.call: One pull number for each harder tier, the same on every ground.
decideFirst.whyFirst: It is the formula form of the tiers and it sets what every ground asks.

decideFirst.call: A gear curve as a game formula, linear in Level, with a band the size of a tier.
decideFirst.whyFirst: The kill reward, uniques, jewelry and every band read it.

decideFirst.call: What a kill pays follows the pace line, with one tier table for every ground.
decideFirst.whyFirst: It sets XP on every ground at once, and the Level table needs it.

decideFirst.call: From Level 50 your table of hours is the Level law and the cost of a Level is derived from it.
decideFirst.whyFirst: Every day number in the game comes from it.

decideFirst.call: Past the third Blessing, a new one opens whenever a fully blessed death would cost over five hours.
decideFirst.whyFirst: It settles two targets you ruled that do not fit together past about Level 100.

decideFirst.call: Tempering, Hallmarks and linings cost a share of a band's gold, sized on an account of four, with early sinks in place of the slots.
decideFirst.whyFirst: Gold needs something to buy from the first week, and the slot ladder is gone.

decideFirst.call: One table, the Path, says when every system opens, and the first hour teaches four heroes.
decideFirst.whyFirst: Four heroes from day 1 makes the first hour the hardest design problem left.

decideFirst.call: One boss door: every boss has a hall and a key, and one key is one prize roll.
decideFirst.whyFirst: World bosses and events will build on the boss system.

decideFirst.call: A hall's prize holds only what no ground drops.
decideFirst.whyFirst: It decides what the end of every region is worth.

decideFirst.call: Three special pieces and a signature stone on three grounds, as the first rare finds a hero keeps.
decideFirst.whyFirst: It is the sample that every later rare item is sized on.

decideFirst.call: An old ground can be hunted at your own Level, with one drop rule.
decideFirst.whyFirst: It is how the world keeps up with Levels that never end.

then: The build plan: once the calls are ruled, one plan orders the work so each formula lands before the systems that read it.
The build: lanes follow that plan, each change proven on the balance matrix before the next one leans on it.
The release: one big release for the beta, then the wipe and Early Access after the full Security review.
